2. The plaintiff-petitioners filed the suit stating inter alias that land measuring 5.10 acres of S.A. Khatian No. 206 belonged to 1Smail and others. Ayub Ali one of the recorded tenants sold .61/2 acre of land to Altafur Rahman and Abeda Khatun on March 29, 1982. Altafur Rahman gifted his purchased land to his wife Abeda Khatun on March 27, 1984. Abeda Khatun sold .61/2acre of land acquired by purchase and gift to plaintiff Nos.1 and 3 on January 30, 1986 and the said plaintiffs, as they claimed. have constructed a tin shed in their purchased land. It is also the case of the plaintiff's that they have purchased .63/4 of land by 3 kabalas of October 13, 1987 form the successive transferees of the recorded tenant Dulamia. It. is the case of the plaintiffs that in the aforesaid manner they have acquired .131/4 acres of land and they arc possessing the land by raising hut. It is also the contention of the plaintiffs that on April 20, 1997 defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the land in suit and as such they are constrained to tile the suit. 

 3. The .suit was contested by defendant No. 1 by filing written statement contending, inter alias that the suit as framed is not maintainable against the co-sharers since there was no partition either by metes and bounds or amicable of the land of plot No.2033 in S. A. Khatian No. 206. Ills specific case is that Ayub Ali had no subsisting interest to transfer .61/2 acre of land to Altafur Rahman and Abeda Khatun, that Ayub Ali's mother Umme Kulsum gifted .26 acre of land to her grand son Farid Uddin son of Ayub Ali by a deed of gift of February 15, 1967 and he (defendant No.1) has purchased .81/8 acre of land of plot No. 2033 listed in S. A. Khatian No. 206 from Farid Uddin by the kabala dated February 25, 1991 and he is in possession thereof, that plaintiffs upon given fictitious boundary are trying to grab his land, that while the plaintiffs tried to erect structure in the land of the plot in question then the local Chairman on April 27, 1997 made order not to erect any structure. 

 4. Trial Court on the findings that plaintiff's have been able to prove their case and that the suit as framed is maintainable and plaintiffs are entitled to have the decree prayed for to restrain the defendants from interfering with their possession decreed the suit. On appeal the appellant Court upon detailed discussions of the materials on record arrived at the findings that from the documents of the plaintiffs it is seen that there is no recital in their documents that they have purchased the land so claimed on the southwestern part of plot No. 2033, nor there is any averment in the kabalas that the plaintiffs' vendors put them into possession in any specific portion of the land of plot No.2033. It was also held by the appellate Court that the lands of the khatian No.206 recorded in 8 plots were never partitioned by metes and bounds among the recorded tenants nor was there any arnica  partition amongst the recorded tenants. The appellate Court on security on the schedule of the plaint and the kabalas held that description of the land given in the plaint does not tally with the description on the land given in the kabalas. The appellate Court thereupon allowed the appeal and on setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissed the suit. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record concurred with the findings and decisions of the appellate Court and thereupon discharged the Rule. 

 5. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court were in error in dismissing the suit although trial Court on a detailed discussions of the evidence of the parties arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their prima facie title to the land in suit and also their possession in the land as regards to which they have sought for a decree of permanent injunction. The leared Counsel further submits that High Court Division as well as the appellate Court were in error in dismissing the suit primarily determining the question of title of the plaintiffs although in a suit for permanent injunction question of title is to be gone into incidentally and the primary point for determination is the question of possession. The undisputed position is that plaintiff's and the defendant No.1 are the co-sharers of the land of plot No. 2033 listed in S. A. khatian No. 206. The total quantity of land in S. A. khatian No. 206 is 5.10 acres comprising 8 plots. The plaintiffs are claiming .131/4 acre of land from the southwestern corner of Plot No. 2033. No material has been brought on record by the plaintiffs to show that their vendors by partition either by metes and bounds or amicable got in plot No.2033 the land as they are claiming on southwestern corner of plot No.2033. It has been noticed by the appellate Court that in plaintiffs kabalas there is no recital that their vendors are in specific possession or the land so transferred on the southwestern corner portion of plot No.2033. Nor there is any recital that vendors have made over possession to the plaintiff the land on the southwestern corner of plot NO. 2033. The appellate Court has also noticed dissimilarity in the description of land claimed by plaintiff' i.e. boundary given in the schedule of the plaint and the land described in the schedule of the kabalas. This finding of the appellate Court sufficiently established the contention of the defendant that plaintiff's by giving fictitious boundary of the land in the schedule of the plaint are trying to grab his land. The learned Counsel for the petitioners could not refer to any material from the record to show that the finding arrived at by the appellate Court as to divergence of the description of the land given in the plaint and the kabalas and that absence of any recital in the plaintiffs'. kabalas that their vendors either upon partition by metes and bounds or by amicable partition were enjoying the land so transferred on the southwestern corner of plot No. 2033. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view that High Court Division as well as the appellate Court were quite correct in arriving at the finding that plaintiffs as co-sharers or the land of plot No.2033 and having not established of being in specific possession of any portion of the land of plot No.2033 can not have a decree for permanent injunction against the other en-sharers when the land of the holding was not partitioned either by metes and bounds or there was amicable partition among the co-sharers. The High Court Division on detailed discussions of the materials on record has concurred with the findings and decisions of the appellate Curt. Since from the side of the 'petitioners no infirmity of the kind has been pointed out in the judgment of the High. Court Division calling fir interference by this Division the petition is liable to be dismissed.
